result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that the three numbers don't show job impact, and both give director wording with a date. B is more direct about n=12 being too small to rule out ordinary variation, and it adds strong onboarding measures such as time to proficiency and retention. A is leaner and handles the delayed check and short-term recall a bit better, but it never states the small-sample limit as clearly as B does. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and an end-of-course quiz don't show better job performance, and both give the director usable wording. A lists more concrete measures, such as time to proficiency and 90-day attrition, but its plan is heavier, its script assumes earlier cohorts exist, and it says the content is 'landing'. B makes a later 30/60-day check part of the plan, notes that a same-day quiz mostly measures short-term recall, and warns against saying the program 'worked', so it edges ahead on honesty and the delayed check.
